subject: Recap + next steps: Upshot k6 rehearsal and SLO alignment
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Lara Kim <lara.kim@upshot.ai>, Jorge Alvarez <jorge.alvarez@upshot.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps: Upshot k6 rehearsal and SLO alignment

Hi Lara / Jorge —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth before the rehearsal: 

Summary of requirements we heard:
- Target SLOs: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 200ms, p99 < 600ms for generation endpoints (1k token median).
- Throughput target: sustained 600 RPS across 3 model routes during the window (burst to 1k for 2–3 minutes).
- Concurrency: target 150 concurrent VUs for k6; for streaming queries we expect ~12 simultaneous streams.
- Streaming expectations: per-chunk latency p50 < 100ms, p99 < 600ms; ensure chunked responses preserved.
- Authentication: we'll use the test API key you provisioned; please confirm test account id and any IP restrictions.

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) Upshot sends IP ranges to allowlist + preferred rehearsal window (we suggested 2028-07-25 02:00–06:00 UTC).
2) Redwood provides the k6 test bundle (scripts + environment file) and a short runbook with exact k6 command lines and thresholds.
3) On the day we run a 30–45 minute warmup + 90 minute sustained window, then a short spike run.
4) Post-run we’ll share raw logs, consolidated SLO heatmap, and suggested mitigations.

Attachments we plan to circulate: runbook-upshot-rehearsal.pdf, script-upshot-k6.tar.gz (Dev will share).

Please reply with the allowlist and confirm the window or propose alternatives. If everything looks good we’ll schedule a 15-min pre-rehearsal sync 24 hours before.

Thanks —
Dylan
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Lara Kim <lara.kim@upshot.ai>

Date: Sun, 22 Jul 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: Upshot k6 rehearsal and SLO alignment

Thanks Dylan — good write-up. Confirming a few things from our side: 

- We can provide the allowlist; attached is a CSV with our egress IPs (allowlist-upshot.csv). Please confirm which port range you need opened (we typically allow 443 outbound).
- Test account: upshot-test-2028 (we will enable the API key this afternoon and share the key via your secure portal).
- Preferred window works for us: 2028-07-25 02:00–06:00 UTC. If you need to shift +/- 2 hours we can accommodate.

Couple of clarifying questions: 
1) For streaming clients, we have customers who open persistent connections — can you confirm your expected connect/idle timeouts so we match load generator behavior?
2) Can Redwood publish a single-run summary with raw latencies (not just percentiles) so we can post-process?

Attaching the allowlist. We’ll follow up with the test API key via the secure channel.

—Lara
Head of Platform, Upshot AI

(attachment: allowlist-upshot.csv)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Lara Kim <lara.kim@upshot.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Jul 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: Upshot k6 rehearsal and SLO alignment

Attaching the bundle (script-upshot-k6.tar.gz) and a brief README here. Key details for the rehearsal run: 

Test topology and commands:
- k6 script: scripts/upshot_stream_and_gen.js (contains both streaming and generation scenarios)
- Recommended command (Linux/mac): 
  K6_RUNNER=local TEST_API_KEY=REDACTED TEST_ACCOUNT_ID=upshot-test-2028 
  k6 run --vus 150 --duration 90m --out json=results.json scripts/upshot_stream_and_gen.js

Load profile notes:
- Warmup: 10m linear ramp from 10 -> 150 VUs
- Sustained window: 90m at 150 VUs (~600 RPS across routes)
- Spike: 3m to 1000 RPS to validate graceful degradation and fallback metrics

Thresholds and expectations (for post-run alerting):
- Generation endpoints: p95 < 200ms, p99 < 600ms
- Streaming chunk latencies: p50 < 100ms, p99 < 600ms; expect increased variance during the spike
- Error budget: < 0.5% 5xx across the sustained window

Streaming-specific notes:
- k6 uses a small helper to maintain persistent HTTP/2 connections for streaming routes; set idle timeout to 300s to match Redwood runtime defaults.
- Maintain 12 concurrent long-poll streams during sustained window. If Upshot plans more streams, please advise and we’ll adjust VUs.

Artifacts attached: script-upshot-k6.tar.gz (scripts + env template), runbook-upshot-rehearsal.pdf (checklist and post-run data delivery).

Let me know if you want me to add a short synthetic that simulates token-size variance (we added a simple generator already).

—Dev
Software Engineer, Performance
Redwood Inference

(attachment: script-upshot-k6.tar.gz; attachment: runbook-upshot-rehearsal.pdf)
